action_tier_matrix.rationale: Lowest current risk, real behavior improving -- the safest, highest-confidence candidates for a meaningful limit increase.
Low current risk, no deterioration signal -- a modest increase is proportionate.
Low current risk, but real behavior deteriorating -- hold and re-evaluate next cycle rather than increase into an emerging trend.
Moderate current risk offset by real improvement -- a small increase rewards the trend without ignoring the absolute level.
Moderate risk, no trend signal either way -- no action is the proportionate default.
Moderate risk and real deterioration together -- a proactive, modest exposure reduction before the trend compounds.
High absolute risk, even if genuinely improving -- not yet safe to increase; held rather than decreased in acknowledgment of the real improving trend.
High risk sustained with no improvement -- a proactive exposure reduction.
Highest current risk AND real deterioration -- the customers an operations team should manually review first, before any automated action, for possible line freeze.

utilization_trend_reinterpretation: This dataset has no true credit-limit or balance-to-limit utilization field (see Section 6). 'Utilization-trend' is honestly reinterpreted as PD_TREND = DYNAMIC_PD (Problem 6, real, current) minus STATIC_PD (Problem 1, real, origination-time) for the same customer.
